analysis.title: Ruminations - Macro, Micro, Markets (2 Nov 2026)
key_insights: Nasdaq fell 5% in the week ended 30 Oct. Market-implied odds of a Democratic sweep rose to 72% (+7 points in 2 days). The backdrop is high rates, falling equities, oil above $100, geopolitical uncertainty, political tail risks and rising CPI, PPI and PCE inflation.

Tech stocks are down $5 trillion of market cap over the last 3 weeks while most of the S&P is up over the last month. Last week Russell beat the S&P and S&P ex-AI beat the S&P. On the day Alphabet lost $500bn of market cap, the S&P fell only 30bps because healthcare, real estate and staples outperformed.

Gross exposure has been very hard to carry for 3 weeks. Spreads including software vs semis, value vs growth, small vs big cap, cyclicals vs defensives and crowding vs breadth were difficult to manage. The dividend yield factor and valuation factor now trade in the 90th and 80th percentiles.

Google missed on revenue and EPS and free cash flow was negative. The stock had its worst move in 20 years, losing $500bn in a day. Amazon's AWS grew 39% (fastest in 5 years) with its highest operating margin ever, but trailing 12-month FCF turned negative and signaled higher capex next year. Intel gave a weak Q4 guide and a cash burn warning for FY26 and fell the most on record.
SOX closed down 7% on Friday and below its 200-day moving average for the first time in a year. Semis forward P/E is back at AI-cycle lows (~16x).

Demand is not the issue (Google cloud doubled, Azure +48%, AWS at its fastest growth in 5 years, chip demand solid). The concern is the cost and time to return on AI capex. The big 4 hyperscalers' combined FCF was $26bn. Amazon long-term debt rose from $66bn to $173bn in 9 months, and Meta raised capital last week.

Investors are shifting from ambition to returns and from capex to cash flow. Approaching catalysts are more Mag 7 earnings, the midterms and next steps on Iran. The author questions why both spenders and recipients of AI capex are falling together, since one party's capex is another's revenue.

Headline index drawdowns since 2020: Covid -25%, Russia/Ukraine -24%, 2024 growth scare -11%, 2025 Liberation Day -12%, 2026 AI disruption and Iran conflict -10%, most recent AI doubts -13%. The index was up 70% from trough to peak coming into last week.

B vs CCC spread hit 8% fewer than 5 times since 1996. On each prior occasion the S&P was at least 11.5% below its 52-week high, and on two occasions near 30% below. Coming into last week the S&P was less than 2% below its high despite the trigger.

The S&P is 3% below its all-time high, but Mag 7 has lost $4 trillion of market cap since Oct 15 and 60% of S&P members are in bear market territory. Drawdowns from highs: Applovin -65%, Western Digital -52%, Oracle -50%, Arm -49%, ServiceNow -37%, Intel -35%, Broadcom -31%, Marvell -30%, Alphabet -28%, Meta -22%.

The author argues the Google sell-off reflects a market view that core search is threatened by AI agents while Google spends heavily on AI. Google and Meta each earned around $200bn from advertising in 2025, which frames their capex ramp as an innovator's dilemma.

Governments face fiscal constraints between populism and spending control. Continued issuance is driven by new spending, debt servicing, inflation and risk premium. If absorption of issuance by productivity, domestic savings and foreign demand goes off track, tax increases or spending cuts become necessary.

Brazil rallied 15% into the election and sold off nearly 30% after an unexpected Lula win. Political tail risk remains elevated (Israel coalition uncertainty, unrest in France, US midterms). The UK budget passed without disturbing Gilts, and the author sees UK relative political stability, defensive sectors and low-but-improving growth as a possible positive.

Cyber names have outperformed the S&P year to date: Okta +155%, Fortinet +138%, CrowdStrike +124%, Palo Alto +116%, Hack Cyber ETF +56%. The author points to the Binance hack and other attacks as evidence of rising cyber risk.

market_movers.rationale: Missed on revenue and EPS with negative FCF. Worst one-day move in 20 years and $500bn of market cap lost. The stock is 28% below its all-time high.

sector_views.rationale: Demand is solid but investors are penalizing AI capex and negative free cash flow. Semis forward P/E is at AI-cycle lows (~16x).
These defensive sectors outperformed and cushioned the S&P on the day Alphabet fell. Investors are chasing defensive and under-owned segments.
Cyber names are well ahead of the S&P YTD, and the author notes rising cyber risk with AI adoption.

earnings_insights: Alphabet reported Q3 2026 (late Oct): missed on revenue and EPS, with negative free cash flow. The stock had its worst move in 20 years.
Amazon reported Q3 2026 (late Oct): AWS grew 39% (fastest in 5 years), highest operating margin ever, trailing 12-month FCF turned negative, and the report signaled higher capex next year.
Intel reported (late Oct): weak Q4 guide and a cash burn warning for FY26. The stock fell the most on record.
Microsoft Azure grew 48% in its latest report. Google Cloud doubled.
Meta raised capital last week, reported as a financing event, with no EPS figure given in this note.
More Mag 7 earnings are still ahead.

tension_points.bull_case: Demand is solid: Google cloud doubled, Azure grew 48%, AWS grew at its fastest rate in 5 years, and chip demand is rock solid. One party's capex is another's revenue, and the base case remains that AI changes everything.
tension_points.bear_case: Hyperscalers are moving from cash printing to cash spending. The big 4's combined FCF was $26bn, Amazon's long-term debt rose from $66bn to $173bn in 9 months, and investors now want returns over ambition.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further earnings where free cash flow and capex guidance disappoint, as with the Google, Amazon and Intel reports, with more Mag 7 earnings still to come.

tension_points.bull_case: The S&P was only 3% below its all-time high and within reach of a new high, with breadth improving.
tension_points.bear_case: B vs CCC hit the 8% spread trigger, which previously coincided with S&P drawdowns of at least 11.5%. Mag 7 has lost $4 trillion since Oct 15 and 60% of S&P members are in bear markets.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An S&P drawdown of at least 11.5% from the 52-week high, as on every previous occasion the B vs CCC spread reached 8%.

theme_stances.key_argument: The AI capex bill came due and investors now want returns over ambition and cash flows over capex.

theme_stances.evidence: Equity can hurt you but debt can kill you.
